title: Steve Jobs on computers as bicycles for the mind, doers who think, and interpersonal computing (WGBH, 1990)
summary: In a 1990 WGBH interview, Jobs explains why computers are a bicycle of the mind, why the Apple II and Mac won by serving people who wanted to use computers rather than learn them, and why the next revolution is networked interpersonal computing. He argues the best makers are both thinkers and doers, and that market research cannot produce non-incremental leaps.

principles.text: Great tools amplify human ability; a computer is a bicycle for the mind.
principles.quote: we humans are tool builders. And that we can fashion tools that amplify these inherent abilities that we have to spectacular magnitudes. And so for me, a computer has always been a bicycle of the mind.

principles.text: Design for people who want to use the tool, not learn how to use it.
principles.quote: most people didn’t want to learn how to use the computer. They just wanted to use it.

principles.text: The best creators are thinkers and doers in one person; claiming the thinking is easy.
principles.quote: the doers are the major thinkers. The people that really create the things that change this industry are both the thinker and doer in one person.

principles.text: Combine art and science, thinking and doing, like Leonardo, to get exceptional results.
principles.quote: combing all of those skills together, the art and the science, the thinking and the doing, was what resulted in the exceptional result.

principles.text: Market research can't invent breakthroughs; use it to check your instincts after you make the jump.
principles.quote: market research can tell you what your customers think of something you show them. Or it can tell you what your customers want as an incremental improvement on what you have but very rarely can your customers predict something that they don’t even quite know they want yet.

principles.text: Technology is a means, not an end; don't lose sight of the real human purpose.
principles.quote: a lot of people have mistaken it as the end rather than the means.
